title: Inadequate turbulent support in low-metallicity molecular clouds
question: Are molecular clouds in the low-metallicity Galactic outer disk and in metal-poor dwarf galaxies in virial equilibrium (virial parameter near unity), as measured from optically thin 13CO?

data.arrays: New data: ALMA Total Power (TP) Array, 26 outer-disk clouds. Archival: ACA (7 m + TP) for SMC (2013.1.00652.S), 12 m array for SMC (2015.1.00581.S) and NGC 6822 (2019.1.01641.S), 12 m / 12 m + TP cubes for LMC from Wong et al. 2019
data.angular_resolution: ALMA TP beam ~29.5 arcsec; SMC cubes restored to 2.0 arcsec (ideal ~1 arcsec); NGC 6822 restored to 2.4 arcsec; LMC cubes 3.5 arcsec
data.sensitivity: ALMA TP typical Tmb,rms ~0.04 K; SMC interferometry cubes ~0.4 K (~0.06 Jy per beam); NGC 6822 ~0.01 K (~0.6 mJy per beam)

what.value: LMC 13CO cubes (12 m, and 12 m + TP for the Planck cold cloud)

evidence.quote: We used the $^{13}$CO cubes provided in the literature(cite: 2019ApJ...885...50W) for several regions in the LMC.

recipe.goal: Reduce single-dish and TP data into cubes
recipe.method: IRAM: GILDAS/CLASS baseline subtraction per FTS200 unit and xy_map gridding; ALMA TP: standard pipeline
key_parameters: IRAM cube pixel size 4 arcsec x 4 arcsec

recipe.goal: Derive cloud distances and Galactocentric radii
recipe.method: BeSSeL Bayesian code from l, b, VLSR; spiral-arm term dropped; kinematic distance from the rotation curve for most outer-disk clouds
assumptions: Heights above the plane negligible (|b| < 4 deg)

recipe.goal: Build source masks in each cube
recipe.method: Source-finding algorithm in 3DBAROLO, with S/N-based growth
key_parameters: MASK=Search, SNRCUT=3, GROWTHCUT=2.5; GRS: THRESHOLD=0.39 K, GROWTHTHRESHOLD=0.33 K

recipe.method: Solve 13CO optical depth per voxel from radiative transfer, integrate over velocity to get N(13CO)
key_parameters: Tex from optically thick 12CO peak where available, else Tex = 15 K
assumptions: 13CO and 12CO share the same Tex; 12CO optically thick; beam filling factor unity; Tbg = 2.73 K

recipe.method: N(H2) = N(13CO) x 12CO/13CO x H2/12CO with radius-dependent ratios for the Galaxy; fixed H2/13CO for LMC, SMC and NGC 6822
key_parameters: 12C/13C = 5.87 Rgc + 13.25; H2/12CO at the solar radius 6.0e3, scaling inversely with O/H
assumptions: 12CO/13CO equals the isotopic 12C/13C ratio; H2/12CO inversely proportional to O/H

recipe.goal: Measure cloud radius, velocity dispersion and mass
recipe.method: Measurements within the half-peak isophote of N(H2); beam-deconvolved equivalent radius, intensity-weighted sigma_v corrected for channel width, mass from integrated N(H2)
key_parameters: Adopted uncertainties: 10% for r_cloud and sigma_v, 20% for M_mol

recipe.goal: Compute virial parameter and its trend with metallicity
recipe.method: alpha_vir = 5 sigma_v^2 R / (G M); galactic metallicity from the O/H gradient; ordinary least-squares fit of log alpha_vir versus log Z
key_parameters: Supervirial: alpha_vir > 1; subvirial: alpha_vir < 1; factor-of-two virial vs equipartition not distinguished
assumptions: Uniform sphere (a = 1); a ~ 1.4 +/- 0.3 for realistic density profiles would lower alpha_vir

recipe.goal: Estimate the magnetic field needed to support subvirial clouds
recipe.method: General virial theorem with magnetic term, assuming efficient ion-neutral momentum transfer; compare required B with B versus nH relation from Zeeman data
key_parameters: Cosmic-ray ionization rate 1e-17 s^-1; ionization fraction ~1e-7; MHD cutoff wavelength <~0.01 pc
assumptions: External pressure neglected in the outer Galaxy; external magnetic field neglected (~10 uG vs ~100 uG required)

score_reason: Public ALMA and figshare data and a fairly complete equation-level recipe with numeric results, but several inputs are blank-cited and imaging details for the ALMA parts are missing.
rediscovery_reason: ALMA TP and archival data are public, the virial-parameter recipe is given in equations, and the main results (alpha_vir versus Z, fit coefficients) are numeric, though some ancillary inputs are not recoverable from the text.
